name: Kouign-amann
origin: Breton for 'butter cake' (kouign, cake; amann, butter), created in Douarnenez, Brittany, in the 1860s; a laminated yeasted dough folded with layers of butter and sugar, the sugar caramelising in the oven's heat.

ingredients.note: laminated in cold, in folded layers, rather than creamed in — the technique, not the total mass, is what makes kouign-amann's crumb, so this bakersPercent is the whole dough's real total butter
folded into the lamination and coating the exterior; caramelises under the oven's heat into the cake's signature crackling crust
see stollen.json for the same caveat: this figure is a nominal yeast-inoculation proxy, not a literal chemical leavening dose

process.name: mix base dough
process.description: mix flour, water, yeast and salt into a smooth dough

process.name: laminate
process.description: fold in a butter block, then repeatedly fold and roll with sugar between the folds

process.name: bake
process.description: bake hot, so the folded sugar layers caramelise into a crackling crust

notes: Real kouign-amann has no egg at all (the crumb sets through gluten development and lamination, not egg protein), a genuine and correctly-modelled zero here. Butter and sugar each near 55% of flour mass, folded in through lamination rather than creamed, is representative of published Breton bakery formulas.
